selectedPNGs.observation: Initial combat view: the dark faceted body, hooked ivory beak, paired wings, talons, and separated tail plumes read together as one Roc silhouette.
Native pass sequence: the body remains connected while the wing pose opens, with no apparent wing or tail mesh explosion in this combat-distance sample.
Before the focused player action resolves: the original head, face, chest mantle, wings, feet, and tail are all visible on the exact spawned owner.
Visible 10-point hit sample: native impact effects overlay the torso, but the articulated wing and body surfaces remain continuous.
Native Roc attack motion: legs, talons, wing roots, extended wing sections, and head stay attached during the airborne pose.
Later attack sample: the head/beak, broad wings, and tail continue to read as a coherent bird rather than detached static decorations.
Death-sequence entry immediately before the heavy-death clip: the still-visible original silhouette remains intact.
Heavy-death sample: the original body has lowered and folded under native animation; no separated limb or unskinned wing is apparent in the reviewed frame.
Late fixture sample: native victory and loot UI obscure much of the frame, while the retained Roc remains visible behind it. This does not establish final corpse or resource lifetime.

limits: This review samples nine stills rather than every rendered pose or camera angle.
Native combat UI, player overlap, hit flashes, and victory/loot UI obscure fine feather, eye, and death detail.
The registered head PortraitCam marker was not separately pixel-captured here; portrait framing remains a distinct gate.
The final death frame is UI-obscured. No claim is made about settled corpse state, ragdoll, culling envelope, material disposal, or completed art direction.
This verdict covers only the fresh rocA/enRoc01 profile, not rocB, jungle Roc variants, or other bird rigs.
